clue.text: Doing away with fighting

definitions.meaning: ... a plan means discarding or abolishing it
slang for brawling, having a scrap

explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to discard it, and a scrap is also a brawl, so the word covers both abolishing and brawling.

clue.text: County Alderman with a sort of round guilelessness

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for County Alderman, an old local-government office

indicators.note: a sort of round says the letters of round are made into a different version of themselves

explanation.surface: A local councillor and his roundabout honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' is the anagram signal on the word after it; 'with' is only a joining word. County Alderman was an old rank on English county councils.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is frankness and openness, the absence of guile or deceit.

clue.text: Ways to look at faces

definitions.meaning: ... of a problem are angles from which it can be viewed
an aspect is also a side or face of a building or object

explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is both a viewpoint on a question and the side a thing presents, such as a house's south-facing front.

clue.text: Diarist, we hear, who transformed "What the Butler saw'"?

indicators.note: we hear says the diarist's name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Samuel Pepys is England's most famous diarist

indicators.note: transformed says the three letters of who are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about a diarist who turned a saucy title into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Pepys is said 'peeps'; 'transformed' turns WHO into HOW. 'What the Butler Saw' was the title of a famous saucy Victorian coin-operated viewing machine at seaside piers.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic 'What the Butler Saw' machines on British piers were viewers showing saucy pictures through an eyehole, the archetypal example of the type.

clue.text: Taxonomic groups not entirely universal

indicators.note: not entirely says the word for universal loses its final letter

parts.note: general means universal, applying to all

explanation.surface: Classification groups that do not quite cover everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are the ranks in biological classification above species, the plural of genus.

clue.text: Sad, losing out in this noted slide

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of sad and losing are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy at losing, set in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SAD and LOSING together; 'in this' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a musical sweep gliding through a run of pitches, so a slide through notes.

clue.text: Idyllic part of Greece?

parts.note: a real mountainous region of the Peloponnese whose name poets made the byword for a rural paradise

explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is both a region of southern Greece and, in pastoral poetry, an idealised unspoilt countryside.

clue.text: Deportment of a nude more outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of a nude more are rearranged

explanation.surface: Comment on the behaviour of a scandalously naked person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges A, NUDE and MORE; 'of' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is a person's outward bearing and behaviour, the way they carry and conduct themselves.

clue.text: Out of shape general in a wax!

indicators.note: out of shape says the letters of general lose their form and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unfit army officer in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wax' looks like temper ('in a wax' is British slang for in a rage), but it is the verb, to grow, as the moon waxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow larger, as the waxing moon does, so it means to increase in size.

clue.text: Turtle and fish photographer?

definitions.meaning: the snapping turtle is commonly called a ...
the red ... is a food fish

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a snapping turtle, a reef fish of that name, and anyone who takes snaps with a camera.

clue.text: Bind some children's lavender

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tying up some of the lavender the children picked.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave someone is to bind them in servitude, holding them captive.

clue.text: Races don't disturb this town

indicators.note: disturb tells us the letters of races don't are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A town whose horse races must go on undisturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturb' rearranges RACES and DONT. Doncaster is a Yorkshire town famous for its racecourse, home of the St Leger, which makes the surface fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is a town in South Yorkshire, England, best known for horse racing.

clue.text: Ravel semi-intent on champagne, for example

indicators.note: semi means half, here the second half of the word intent

parts.note: champagne is one kind of sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Ravel half absorbed in a glass of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer, but it is the verb, to tangle; 'semi' takes the back half of INTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or twist threads together, as to entwine them.

clue.text: Swimming race includes all techniques initially

indicators.note: includes says one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letters of all and techniques

explanation.surface: A swimming event that features every stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like part of the swimming picture, but it means a people, NATION, which holds AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Natation is a formal word for swimming, from the Latin for to swim.

clue.text: Preston North End gone-at great speed

indicators.note: end gone says the closing letter of the town's name is removed

parts.note: taken as written, the Lancashire town

explanation.surface: The football club Preston North End departing in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston North End is an English football club; here its final N (North) is removed from PRESTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction meaning very fast.

clue.text: In favour of light-weight schedule?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a gramme is a very light unit of weight

explanation.surface: Supporting a lighter timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a planned timetable of events, so a schedule.

clue.text: Moroccan in loose jacket that can be peeled off

definitions.meaning: a native of Tangier in Morocco

definitions.text: in loose jacket that can be peeled off
definitions.meaning: a small citrus fruit with a loose skin that peels away easily

explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit was named for Tangier, and someone from that Moroccan city is likewise called by that name.

clue.text: Lumbering hostile type at precinct

annotationWithheld.why: 'Lumbering hostile type at precinct': WARD is precinct and lumbering defines AWKWARD, but 'hostile type' does not give AWK; probably OCR damage (perhaps a beheaded HAWK) and no source found.

clue.text: Irregular composition had prosy translation

indicators.note: translation turns the words had prosy into a new form, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A dull rendering of an ill-formed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-form, episodic musical work without a strict structure.

clue.text: A look back at grave sort of lottery

parts.note: a grave is a tomb

indicators.note: back says the words a look are read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A backward glance at a burial place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only 'A look' around; 'at' just joins it to the grave. Lo is the archaic exclamation meaning look or behold.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle where tickets are drawn from a revolving drum, popular at British fetes.

clue.text: Monkey's blunder

explanation.definitionFit: A howler monkey is named for its call, and a howler is also an embarrassing error.

clue.text: Bird arrived and blew out of tune!

indicators.note: out of tune says the letters are jumbled, like notes gone wrong

parts.note: arr is the abbreviation for arrived, as on timetables

explanation.surface: A bird turns up and plays a sour note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of tune' rearranges ARR and BLEW together.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbler is any of many small songbirds, and the word fits a singer.

clue.text: Appeal to England's openers to entertain

parts.note: the first two letters of the word England
to treat someone is to entertain them at your expense

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen appeal to the crowd for entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly with someone.

clue.text: American, Russian or English style of architecture

definitions.meaning: a native of the US state of Georgia
a native of Georgia, once a Soviet republic
the style of the reigns of the four Kings George, 1714 to 1830

explanation.definitionFit: Two places called Georgia supply people, and the four King Georges gave their name to an 18th-century architectural style.

clue.text: A party colour much loved

parts.note: a do is a party
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A party in one colour that everyone cherished.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply and devotedly.

clue.text: Dangerous sort of speed to censure

indicators.note: sort of says the letters of speed are made into another arrangement

parts.note: to rate is an old verb meaning to scold or berate

explanation.surface: Speeding is a perilous thing to criticise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' is the anagram signal on 'speed'; 'to' is a joining word. Rate in the sense of scold survives mainly in the longer word berate.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate criminal is reckless and liable to violence, so dangerous.

clue.text: Inn requiring a pound, therefore

parts.note: pound gives LB
ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A tavern that charges a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: An albergo is an Italian inn or hotel.

clue.text: Long-haired dog right for a pitman?

parts.note: the collie is a long-coated sheepdog

explanation.surface: Asking whether a shaggy dog suits a miner.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, one who works down a pit.

clue.text: Give me angel-mix for a salmagundi

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir the letters of me and angel together

explanation.surface: A request to a heavenly being to toss a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' rearranges ME and ANGEL. A salmagundi is a mixed salad, hence any miscellany.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or medley, as a salmagundi is a jumble of assorted ingredients.

clue.text: Remove moisture with dry heated process

indicators.note: process means the letters of dry heated are worked into new form

explanation.surface: Drying something out by heating it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate is to draw water out of something, drying it.
